doc.title: Bobby Gordon interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997

title: How long recording sessions take
summary: Making a CD takes two or three days, about two on the Marty Grosz albums.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: When you make recordings these days, how long do you usually get in the studio to do a record?

Well it takes us about two or three days maybe to make one record. Sometimes you can make one in one day, sometimes it takes two or three days. A lot of musicians shuffling back and forth and you have to wait for them, some of them are busy on the one day and you have to come in the next day. But all and all it’s quite — especially with making CDs — it’s quite a lot of work to do that because it takes about two or three days. On the Marty Grosz albums that I’ve made we usually take about two days on those.
